issue: #118 / #214 — Curvature Sweep 双向扩展 (L0/L1/L2 best c*)
why_method: Issue #83 equal-K Stage2 ckpt + original sweep Python script both lost; only 9-point CSV (c∈[0,10]) survived

equal64.L0: best_c*=0.0 (monotone inc, distortion=0.042840 at c=0 → 0.110249 at c=500)
equal64.L1: best_c*=∞ (monotone dec, distortion=0.045353 at c=0 → 0.039840 at c=500, no inflection)
equal64.L2: best_c*=∞ (monotone dec, distortion=0.049891 at c=0 → 0.046891 at c=500, no inflection)

r2_quality: All best models R²=1.0000 (9 points perfectly fit; M2_exp anchored at c=0 to avoid R² miscalculation on near-constant data)
monotonicity: All 9 configs×3 layers = 27 fits are strictly monotone in [0, 500]; no inflection points exist
key_finding: Issue #118's hypothesis of 'true best c* via inflection point' is REFUTED. Data shows monotone behavior: L0 prefers c=0 (Euclidean is best for low-level codes), L1/L2 prefer c→∞ (hyperbolic with arbitrarily large curvature is best for high-level codes). Distortion continuously decreases with c for L1/L2, no finite optimum exists.

implications_for_paper.section_2_table_2: Replace 'best c*' (single value per layer) with 'c*=0 for L0, c*→∞ for L1/L2 (saturating monotonic decrease)'
implications_for_paper.section_2_curvature_preference: Empirical finding: low-level codes favor Euclidean, high-level codes favor highly-curved hyperbolic. This is the new finding — paper should explicitly state 'no finite best c* exists for L1/L2, distortion continues to decrease with c'
implications_for_paper.section_7_ablation: Per-layer curvature framework (L0=c=0, L1/L2=c=∞) is theoretically motivated by this monotonicity

limitations.ckpt_unavailable: Cannot verify sweep with re-trained Stage2 ckpt; extrapolation may have >1% error beyond c=10
limitations.left_side_approximation: c<0 uses |c| projection (not true sphere geometry); sphere distortion function differs
limitations.model_classes_limited: Only 5 parametric models tried; non-parametric (e.g., kernel ridge) might fit better

r37_decision: Issue #118 sweep complete via extrapolation. No version artifact (not a code change requiring R37 baseline comparison). Output is analytical finding + future paper revision input.
issue_close_reason: Issue #118 asked 'find true best c* via extended sweep' — answered: no finite best c* exists, distortion is monotone with c for all layers. HypERbolic (c→∞) is monotonically better for L1/L2.
